title: Wringer gate assertion observations
description: `gate-assertions.json` — what each gate that declared `evidence: {kind: assertions}` actually reported, translated from its own runner's output. A SIBLING of manifest.json like checks.json, selection.json and stability.json, ABSENT when no gate declared structured evidence, which is every bundle written before this existed. **The question it exists to answer.** An exit code says whether a command succeeded. It does not say whether a single assertion ran. Measured with real runners on 19 September 2026: `node --test --test-reporter=tap` over two skipped tests exits **0** and reports `# pass 0, # skipped 2`, so a gate whose whole testimony is its exit code passes on a suite that asserted nothing; and `playwright test --reporter=json` with its browser binary absent exits 1 reporting `stats.unexpected: 2` and **two specs with status `failed`**, with an empty top-level `errors` array — indistinguishable, in the runner's own JSON, from two product assertions that failed. The only trace of the real cause is inside an error MESSAGE. **Two facts, kept apart.** `status` is whether this run established anything: `unavailable` means it did not, which is a different claim from a product assertion that failed, and a gate whose observation is `unavailable` cannot pass however it exited. `classification` is whether the shortfall was the environment's: `environment` is set only from measurements this supervisor made itself — a shell that exited 126 or 127 and so could not execute the command, a timeout, a gate that produced no readable report at all, or the bounded browser launch probe of `requires:` reporting that the declared engine does not start on this host. **It is never set from log text**, because a message is what the failing thing chose to say. An `environment` failure is also excluded from red-first receipts: a browser that could not start never demonstrated that a check can fail. **What it does not claim.** Executed assertions are not honest or sufficient assertions, and a translated identity is the runner's own test name, so renaming a test changes it — which is the point, since the comparison a receipt makes is between the same assertions. Its absence means *no gate declared structured evidence*, never *every gate asserted something*.

gates.description: One row per attempt of each gate that declared `evidence:`, in execution order. A gate with a `stability:` policy contributes one row per attempt, because a flaky gate's attempts are separate observations.

adapter.description: Which runner's report was translated. Wringer reads these three formats and refuses to parse arbitrary output, because a parser for everything is a parser nobody can trust.

source.description: Where the report came from: the gate's captured stdout, or the repository-relative path its own command was declared to write.

status.description: `established`: assertions executed and the report agrees with the observed exit. `unavailable`: this run established nothing about the requirement — an empty or all-skipped suite, a report contradicting the exit code, a declared requirement the report omitted, a runner error, or no readable report at all.

classification.description: `assertions`: whatever happened, the runner's own assertions are what happened. `environment`: the supervisor measured that the run could not have produced a product assertion. Only four things set it, all of them this supervisor's own observations: exit 126 or 127 from the shell, a timeout, no readable report, or a launch probe reporting that the declared browser does not start here.

counts.description: The translated totals, or null when no report could be read. `executed` is total minus skipped and is the number the `established` rule turns on: zero executed assertions cannot pass.

requirements.description: The criteria this gate's `proves:` binds, which are what its assertions are evidence FOR. Empty when the gate binds none, in which case no `wringer-check.v1` report is written — assertions with nothing to be evidence of have no requirement mapping to record — and only the counts above speak.

assertions.description: Every translated assertion, with the runner's own test name beside the derived id. The name lives here and not in the frozen `wringer-check.v1` report, whose id pattern cannot hold a sentence.

observation.description: The path of this attempt's `wringer.check-observation.v1` record — the same format the contained lane's protected runners produce, so one reader serves both. Null when the gate binds no criterion.

report_sha256.description: sha256 of the canonical `wringer-check.v1` report, or null when none was produced.

reason.description: The sentence a person reads: the rule that decided `status`, followed by the measurement that decided `classification` when one did.

limits.description: What this record does NOT claim, travelling with it. Pinned by CONTENT in the tests.
